content.text: The text surveys gastric anomalies and rupture, rejecting “gastromalacia” as a disease occurring during life. It then explains intestinal digestion, emphasizing bile, pancreatic and intestinal juices, absorption, and causes of intestinal indigestion such as diet, anemia, stress, sedentary habits, constipation, and disease of the liver or pancreas. Symptoms include delayed abdominal pain, gas, altered stools, malnutrition, anemia, nervous disturbances, and wasting; treatment centers on rest, regulated meals, careful mastication, exercise, climate change, bathing, milk-based diets, and limited medicines. Constipation is defined as prolonged or difficult evacuation, caused by diet, inactivity, disease, habit, or obstruction, and may produce fecal impaction, dilation, ulcers, and systemic symptoms. Enteralgia, intestinal catarrh, chronic diarrhea, cholera morbus, and summer diarrhea in children are also described, with emphasis on hygiene, safe food and water, breastfeeding, cooling, rest, and supportive treatment. Recommended travel includes trips to Europe, seashores, mountains, and therapeutic springs in Virginia or Arkansas.
